finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl lets any remote client read arbitrary files readable by the server process (e.g. /etc/passwd, application secrets, keys) by supplying '../' sequences in the 'f' query parameter.
finding.source: files.go:12 - r.URL.Query().Get("f"), fully attacker-controlled, no validation.
finding.sink: files.go:13 - os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)), returned verbatim to the client at files.go:18 via w.Write(data).

trace.note: /dl is registered with http.HandleFunc on the default mux, no auth middleware
Server listens on ":8082" (all interfaces), handler is reachable without credentials
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd"; ReadFile opens it
File contents written to the HTTP response body

finding.guards_checked: filepath.Join cleans the path but does not confine it to root (it resolves '..' and escapes /srv/files). No filepath.Clean+prefix check, no filepath.Base, no rejection of '..' or absolute paths, no symlink resolution check, no authentication or authorization on the handler or route. An absolute 'f' is concatenated under root, so only '../' sequences escape. Error path (lines 14-16) only returns 404 and does not change exploitability.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /dl handler (files.go:11-19) has no auth and no containment check. filepath.Join at files.go:13 cleans '..' but does not confine the result to root, and the error path (files.go:14-16) only returns 404. The avatar handler's filepath.Base (files.go:22) does not apply to /dl.
verdict.reason: Anonymous clients can reach /dl through the default mux (files.go:32, served on :8082 at files.go:34), and filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") resolves to /etc/passwd, which os.ReadFile at files.go:13 opens and files.go:18 returns to the client, with no effective control in between.
